roles.title: 内閣総理大臣 — Prime Minister of Japan

holder_claims.name: 海部俊樹
holder_claims.note: First appointment (10 August 1989 on the Kantei's retrospective page) lies before the period. Observed on 19 January 1990 signing the Cabinet's written answer No. 1 of the 117th session to the House of Councillors as 内閣総理大臣 海部俊樹: the earliest 1990 attestation pinned to a byte-stable response; the House of Representatives' answer of 23 January 1990 is a second. The acting Prime Minister's signature of 12 January 1990 (橋本龍太郎, 臨時代理) is a claim on the role, not this holder.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the appointment predates the period and no appointment instrument was reviewed, and no source states the day this appointment ended. The notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse and both Houses' designations of 27 February 1990 are claims on the role; the Kantei's span to 28 February 1990 is a retrospective claim only; the reappointment after the election is not used as this end.

holder_claims.name: 海部俊樹
holder_claims.note: Observed on 2 March 1990, when he told both Houses in his policy speech that after the general election he had been appointed Prime Minister again (再び内閣総理大臣に任命され). Both Houses had designated him on 27 February 1990 (claims, never a start); he notified the Cabinet's resignation en masse as Prime Minister on 5 November 1991 (a claim).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the speeches give no date for the reappointment; the second cabinet's formation on 28 February 1990 rests only on retrospective claims (the Kantei page, the House of Councillors' table and a member's remark in debate), and no record of the 1990 Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day this appointment ended; the 5 November 1991 notice and 宮澤喜一's designation are not used as an end.

holder_claims.name: 宮澤喜一
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 5 November 1991 (claims); observed on 8 November 1991, when he told both Houses in his policy speech that he had now been appointed Prime Minister (このたび、私は、内閣総理大臣に任命され).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the 5 November 1991 formation rests on retrospective claims (the Kantei page, the House of Councillors' table and a minister's remark), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 5 August 1993 and 細川護煕's designation are claims, and no source states that he continued to perform the duties until 9 August 1993.

holder_claims.name: 細川護煕
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 6 August 1993 (claims); observed on 23 August 1993, when he told both Houses in his first policy speech that he had now been appointed Prime Minister. A minister's and a member's later remarks that he gave an instruction as Prime Minister on 9 August and visited the Kagoshima disaster area on 13 August are claims dated by the day they recall, never holder dates. The House of Councillors' table and the Houses' written answers of August-September 1993 print 細川護熙 (熙); the Diet minutes and the Kantei print 細川護煕, the form used here.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: the 9 August 1993 formation rests on retrospective claims and a minister's remark, and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 25 April 1994 and 羽田孜's designation are claims, and no record shows him performing the duties between 25 and 28 April 1994.

holder_claims.name: 羽田孜
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 25 April 1994 (claims); observed on 10 May 1994, when he told both Houses that he had been appointed Prime Minister (このたび、私は、内閣総理大臣に任命されました); the House of Representatives' record misprints the speaker label as 内目総理大臣.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 28 April 1994 rests on the Kantei's retrospective list and a member's recollection (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse (decided 25 June 1994) and 村山富市's designation are claims, and no record shows him performing the duties between 25 and 30 June 1994.

holder_claims.name: 村山富市
holder_claims.note: Designated by both Houses on 29 June 1994 (the House of Representatives in a runoff; claims); observed on 18 July 1994, speaking as 内閣総理大臣 in his policy speech. Members referred to the 村山内閣 and to 村山総理 in committee on 6 July 1994; those references are claims and do not date this holder.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 30 June 1994 rests only on his own recollection of 9 November 1994 and the Kantei's retrospective list (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the notice of his Cabinet's resignation en masse of 11 January 1996 and 橋本龍太郎's designation are claims.

holder_claims.name: 橋本龍太郎
holder_claims.note: From 11 January 1996: the Kantei's statement titled 橋本内閣総理大臣談話 and dated that day opens 'I have today taken on the heavy responsibility of Prime Minister' (私は、本日、内閣総理大臣の重責を担うことになりました); the capture's original Last-Modified is 17 January 1996. Both Houses designated him that day (claims), and the same page carries his instructions at that day's first cabinet meeting (a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 7 November 1996 and his re-designation and new appointment that day are not used as this end. The start is day-only: the statement gives no hour and does not describe the appointment ceremony, of which no 1996 record was accessible. His own later recollections (8 November 1996 and 30 July 1998) are retrospective claims, not the basis of the start.

holder_claims.name: 橋本龍太郎
holder_claims.note: Observed on 8 November 1996, when 橋本総理 held the press conference after forming the second Hashimoto cabinet and set out its priorities 'as Prime Minister' (内閣総理大臣として). Both Houses re-designated him on 7 November 1996 (claims). The Kantei statement dated 7 November 1996 says the Prime Minister 'again' took on the office that day, but it prints no name, and its identity rests on the next day's press conference, so it is a claim on the role and not this holder's start.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: no same-day source that names him states the day of the November 1996 reappointment, and no record of the ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended; the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 30 July 1998, his statement of that day that he had decided to resign the office and 小渕恵三's designation are claims, not an end.

holder_claims.name: 小渕恵三
holder_claims.note: The House of Representatives designated him on 30 July 1998 and the House of Councillors designated 菅直人; the joint committee reached no agreement, and under Constitution art. 67(2) the Representatives' designation became the Diet's resolution (claims). Observed on 31 July 1998 in the Kantei's record headed 小渕内閣総理大臣記者会見録. His spoken remark there that 'today' he had come to bear responsibility as Prime Minister is contradicted by his statement in the same record that the new cabinet was launched the previous day, so it is not read as an assumption statement; the unnamed written statement of 31 July says 'on this occasion' (この度), with no day.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No start and no end: 30 July 1998 rests on his next-day recollection, a dated photo caption and the Kantei's retrospective list (claims), and no record of the Imperial appointment ceremony was accessible. No source states the day his office ended: the Cabinet judged on 4 April 2000 that he was 'lacking' under Constitution art. 70 and resigned en masse, and the acting Prime Minister and 森喜朗's appointment followed; none of these is used as an end.

holder_claims.name: 森喜朗
holder_claims.note: From 5 April 2000: the statement dated that day under the heading 森内閣総理大臣演説等 says he was appointed Prime Minister that day (本日、内閣総理大臣に任命され); the Kantei's account names 森喜朗 and says 森総理 was appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that night; the April 2000 cabinet list's profile gives 平成１２年４月５日内閣総理大臣. The Imperial Household Agency's schedule records a 親任式・認証官任命式 that day without naming the appointee (jp_kunaicho_ceremony_20000405, a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 4 July 2000, his re-designation and his reappointment that night are not used as this end. The start is day-only; no clock time is stored.

holder_claims.name: 森喜朗
holder_claims.note: From 4 July 2000: the Kantei's account 第２次森内閣発足 says 森総理 was re-designated that afternoon and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that night as the 86th Prime Minister. His statement of that day ('本日、再び内閣総理大臣の重責を担うことになりました') prints no name, and the Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee; both are claims on the role.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day his office ended; the notices of the Cabinet's resignation en masse and his statement of 26 April 2001 that the Mori cabinet resigned that day, and 小泉純一郎's appointment that night, are not used as an end. The Kantei's span to 26 April 2001 is a retrospective claim.

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 26 April 2001: the Kantei's account 小泉内閣発足 names 小泉純一郎, designated that afternoon, and says that night he attended (臨みました) the Prime Minister's appointment ceremony and the ministers' attestation at the Palace and then issued the Prime Minister's statement, which it quotes. That statement ('本日、内閣総理大臣に任命され') prints no name, and the Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee; both are claims on the role.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 19 November 2003 and his re-designation and reappointment that day are not used as this end. The account says he attended the ceremony rather than that he was appointed; the appointment itself is stated by the unnamed statement it quotes.

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 19 November 2003: the Kantei's account 第二次小泉内閣の発足, dated that day, says 小泉総理 was re-designated and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony as the 88th Prime Minister, and his statement of that day (breadcrumb 小泉総理の演説・記者会見等) says he had again taken on the office that day. The Imperial Household Agency's schedule records the ceremony that day without naming the appointee (a claim on the role).
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no source states the day this appointment ended; the notice of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 21 September 2005 and his reappointment that day are not used as this end. The account dates the ceremony through its date heading and the order of events (その後).

holder_claims.name: 小泉純一郎
holder_claims.note: From 21 September 2005: the Kantei's account 第３次小泉内閣の発足 says 小泉総理 was designated as the 89th Prime Minister and appointed at the Imperial appointment ceremony that day; his statement (breadcrumb 小泉総理の演説・記者会見等) says he had for the third time taken on the office that day; and the Imperial Household Agency's photo page for that day names the ceremony 親任式（小泉内閣総理大臣）. In office on 25 September 2006, when he gave the last interview of his term at the Prime Minister's Office.
holder_claims.uncertainty: No end: no contemporaneous source states the day his office ended. The notices of the Cabinet's resignation en masse of 26 September 2006, his statement that the Koizumi cabinet resigned that day, 安倍晋三's designation and appointment that night (this packet's closing boundary) and the Kantei's retrospective span to 26 September 2006 are claims, not an end; no source states that he continued to perform the duties until the successor's appointment.

roles.scope_note: 内閣総理大臣, the Prime Minister of Japan, head of government under the Constitution of Japan: designated by a resolution of the Diet (art. 67) and appointed by the Emperor (art. 6) at the Imperial appointment ceremony (親任式). CLAUDE-C01-12 keeps each House's designation vote, any joint committee and the House of Representatives' prevailing resolution, the Imperial appointment ceremony, the Prime Minister's same-day statements, a cabinet's formation, the notice of a cabinet's resignation en masse (総辞職), any continued performance of duties until a successor is appointed (art. 71) and an acting prime minister (臨時代理) as separate dated claims. A holder has a start only where a same-day source that names the holder states the day of appointment or assumption of office (a Kantei statement or account, or the Imperial Household Agency's record of the ceremony), and an end only where a source states the day the office ended; no source reviewed does, so no holder has an end. Otherwise a holder is dated by attested_on, from a same-day act in office. A designation vote, a resignation en masse, a successor's designation or appointment and a cabinet's formation are never a boundary; continued performance of duties and acting service are recorded as claims, never as a separate holder of this role.
